classification.difficultyReason: Find the remaining fraction from four unrelated denominators, recover the total from a known remainder, then calculate each daily quantity.

content.prompt:
In a cricket test match, $\frac{1}{6}$ of the runs were scored in the first day, $\frac{1}{5}$ in the second day, $\frac{2}{5}$ in the third day, $\frac{7}{32}$ in the fourth day and remaining 21 runs on the last day.

How many runs were scored on each day?

answer.short: Day 1: 240 runs; Day 2: 288 runs; Day 3: 576 runs; Day 4: 315 runs; Day 5: 21 runs.
answer.worked:
The fraction scored on day 5 is
$$\begin{align*}
f_5 &= 1-\left(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{2}{5}+\frac{7}{32}\right)\\
&=1-\left(\frac{80}{480}+\frac{96}{480}+\frac{192}{480}+\frac{105}{480}\right)\\
&=1-\frac{473}{480}\\
&=\frac{7}{480}.
\end{align*}$$
Let $x$ be the total number of runs.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{7}{480}x &=21\\
x &=21\times\frac{480}{7}\\
&=1440.
\end{align*}$$
The daily totals are
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Day 1} &=\frac{1}{6}\times1440=240\text{ runs}\\
\text{Day 2} &=\frac{1}{5}\times1440=288\text{ runs}\\
\text{Day 3} &=\frac{2}{5}\times1440=576\text{ runs}\\
\text{Day 4} &=\frac{7}{32}\times1440=315\text{ runs}\\
\text{Day 5} &=21\text{ runs}.
\end{align*}$$
